next_step: Finalize SLA for min tokens/sec, agree burst policy, legal sign-off on terms
notes:
Account summary: Sable Orbit builds in-cockpit and ground-station assistants for small satellite operators. Priorities: deterministic throughput, predictable unit cost, and strict audit trails.

Recent timeline / activity bullets:
- 2025-09-15: Intro discovery call (Maya/Ethan) — high-level requirements captured. Customer stressed: 'We need guarantees, not best-effort.'
- 2025-09-29: Product demo — showed dedicated pools, routing policies, and rollback. Positive reaction to canary rollouts.
- 2025-10-02: Stress test (POC) with synthetic telemetry streams — initial numbers: peak observed 4.2k tokens/sec across 6 reserved GPUs (p50 latency ~80ms, p95 ~290ms).
- 2025-10-06: Follow-up call — Sable Ops asked for a hard min throughput commitment of 5k tokens/sec with p95 latency <= 250ms for 1k-context generations.
- 2025-10-09: Legal / procurement kickoff; shared draft SLA + pricing options.

Use-case & technical requirements (from SE notes):
- Workload: interactive flight-assist chat + batch reranking for telemetry search. Typical request size 512-1024 tokens output, steady-state sessions ~120 concurrent, peak bursts up to ~300 concurrent for launch windows.
- Target SLOs: p95 token generation latency <= 250ms at agreed concurrency; 99.9% uptime for inference endpoints; sustained min throughput guarantee of 5,000 tokens/sec across Dedicated pool.
- Concurrency planning: baseline concurrency cap set at 150 sessions. We recommended capacity for 200 concurrent to allow headroom.
- Burst policy request: customer wants automatic burst up to 2x guaranteed throughput for 10 minutes per zone (max 10 minutes per hour) with pre-warmed standby nodes. Pricing impact to be defined (commit premium).
- Fallback behavior: must support deterministic fallback to a quantized 7B family model with graceful degradation (latency SLOs relaxed) if Dedicated pool is saturated. Clear routing policy required.
- Reservation ask: initial reserved GPU footprint proposal = 8x A100-80GB equiv (or equivalent Ampere instances) with autoscale ceiling at 12 GPUs. Preliminary throughput mapping: 8 GPUs -> expected steady tokens/sec ~5.5k with our current kernels/quantization.

SLA negotiation points (open):
- Definition of "min tokens/sec": per-cluster sustained measurement window (5m rolling) vs per-region guarantees. Customer insists on cluster-wide minimum.
- Measurement methodology: p95 latency measured at token level with 99th percentile outliers excluded? SE recommends standard p95 at application ingress. Need legal to define thresholds and remedies.
- Remedies: service credits vs monetary rebates for missed throughput targets. Customer prefers monetary rebate tied to sustained shortfall > 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Burst policy: how to detect and authorize bursts (token-based billing vs capacity-based). Also need guardrails to avoid noisy-neighbor impacts.

POC & acceptance criteria:
- Run a 72-hour soak with representative telemetry and dialog episodes. Acceptance if sustained >=5k tokens/sec for 95% of measurement windows and p95 latency <=250ms.
- Include end-to-end latency checks from Sable's edge to inference endpoint (network path) as part of acceptance.

Commercial notes:
- Two pricing paths under discussion: commit-to-throughput (discounted unit price, higher penalty for overage) vs commit-to-VMs/GPU (simpler capacity reservation). Legal prefers GPU-reservation; Product team favors throughput-commit for clearer unit economics.
- Customer budget target: $250k-$750k ARR first-year, scale later.

Open action items (short):
- SE (Ethan): provide updated perf projection matrix for 6/8/10/12 GPUs, including p95 tokens/sec and latency at 512/1024 context sizes. Due 2025-10-16.
- AE (Maya): finalize commercial terms with pricing options and draft SLA for legal. Due 2025-10-20.
- Infra (Redwood): run isolated stress test for Sable's sample trace to validate headroom and burst behavior. Ticket INF-4327.

Quotes from customer: 'We can't accept soft promises — we operate launches; deterministic throughput matters.'

Next steps: align on measurement definition for min tokens/sec, confirm burst policy (2x for 10 minutes) and trade-off with price, legal review of SLA, pilot sign-off after 72-hour soak.
